record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Topology of Manifolds
record.original_question: Let Sigma be an integral homology 3-sphere that is not homeomorphic to S^3. Does there exist a locally flat embedding Sigma -> S^4 such that one or both complementary regions are not simply connected?

evidence.quote: Question. Let Sigma be an integral homology 3-sphere, not homeomorphic to S3. Is there a locally flat embedding Sigma -> S4 such that one or both complementary regions are not simply-connected?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be an integral homology 3-sphere, i.e., a closed connected oriented 3-manifold with $H_*(\Sigma;\mathbb{Z}) \cong H_*(S^3;\mathbb{Z})$, and assume that $\Sigma$ is not homeomorphic to $S^3$. A continuous embedding $j:\Sigma \hookrightarrow S^4$ is called locally flat if every point $p \in j(\Sigma)$ has an open neighborhood $U$ in $S^4$ together with a homeomorphism $(U, U\cap j(\Sigma)) \cong (\mathbb{R}^4,\mathbb{R}^3)$. By a theorem of Freedman, every such $\Sigma$ admits a locally flat embedding into $S^4$, and for any such embedding $j$, the complement $S^4 \setminus j(\Sigma)$ has exactly two connected components $X$ and $Y$ whose closures are compact topological 4-manifolds with boundary $\Sigma$. 

Question: Does there exist a locally flat embedding $j:\Sigma \hookrightarrow S^4$ such that at least one (or both) of the two complementary regions $X, Y$ has non-trivial fundamental group, i.e., is not simply connected?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in recent work surveying locally flat embeddings of 3-manifolds in $S^4$ (Hillman, 2024) as an open question. Freedman's theorem guarantees that every integral homology 3-sphere embeds locally flatly in $S^4$ and bounds a contractible topological 4-manifold (so simply-connected complementary regions exist), but whether non-simply-connected complementary regions can be realized for $\Sigma \neq S^3$ is listed among open problems. No resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Locally flat embeddings of 3-manifolds in S^4 (J. Hillman)
status_evidence.snippet: Freedman showed that every homology 3-sphere embeds as a locally flat submanifold of S^4 ... the final appendix contains a number of open questions.
status_evidence.claim: The topic of complementary-region fundamental groups for embeddings of homology 3-spheres is actively studied and includes open questions.

status_evidence.title: Locally Flat Embeddings of 3-Manifolds in S^4 (Cambridge book)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies embeddings of 3-manifolds with various complementary fundamental groups (abelian, nilpotent).
status_evidence.claim: The realizability of complementary fundamental groups for embeddings of homology 3-spheres remains a research topic without a known general resolution.
